title: More or Less Wrong: A Benchmark for Directional Bias in LLM Comparative Reasoning

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM reasoning on comparative math word problems systematically varied with different comparative terms ('more', 'less', 'equal') and prompt positions to measure how semantic framing causes directional reasoning errors.

Substituting neutral placeholders with gendered terms ('man', 'woman') in comparative math scenarios to measure how demographic identity cues alter directional error rates (DirErr) and interact with linguistic framing across different activity categories.

Replacing individual placeholders with racial and ethnic descriptors ('White', 'Black', 'Asian', 'Hispanic', 'African') in math word problems to evaluate shifts in directional reasoning drift and non-linear interactions with comparative cues.
